story: Noah builds the ark (SERIES.md episode 8; arc 2, Brothers and the walk with God)
people: The scoffer (characters.json, an invented antagonist, DRAFT until his reference sheet is reviewed; this plan is built only after he is APPROVED) is the valley's ringleader: he opens on screen speaking a taunt in our own words (kind story, no reference: Genesis records no word of the mockers, and none is presented as Scripture) and leads the torch mob at the climax. Noah is DRAFT: only a faceless old man seen from behind or in silhouette, his sons three young men in silhouette; the rest of the mockers are anonymous crowds seen from behind or in silhouette and never speak. The only verses that touch those years are Matthew 24:38 (eating and drinking until the day he entered the ark) and 1 Peter 3:20 (God waited while the ark was a preparing). God is never shown: His lines (Genesis 6:17 right after the taunt, Genesis 6:18 at the turn) are a deep voice-over over storm and lightning. One establishing shot (2 s). The Keeper only for the insight, the comment question and the close.
beats: structure bible-story-short (script.beats): cold_open s-taunt (the scoffer on screen mocks the hull on dry ground, Noah working behind him), then God's Genesis 6:17 (s-voice, voice-over: the flood is real); stake and open loop (years before, one man picked up an axe; how long can he keep building while everyone mocks him?); escalation in three rising steps of the mockers, acted, each ending on a hook (laughter at the size; scorn while the world feasts; stones and cut ropes at night, and God waited); God speaks Genesis 6:18 (s-covenant, voice-over), then the acted climax s-torches (the scoffer leads the mob with torches, Noah keeps hammering) and Genesis 6:22; payoff (the finished ark, the valley goes quiet); keeper_close (insight: Noah never speaks, his sermon was the ark; comment question; part 9).

narration.text: Years before that laugh, one man heard those words, and picked up an axe. On dry ground. Far from any sea.
The whole valley came to laugh. How long can one family keep building while everyone they know mocks them?
Make thee an ark of gopher wood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch.
Genesis does not record what the neighbours said. It does not have to. Picture a ship going up in a dry valley, days from any water.
And this is the fashion which thou shalt make it of: The length of the ark shall be three hundred cubits, the breadth of it fifty cubits, and the height of it thirty cubits.
Three hundred cubits. About four hundred and fifty feet. Every beam cut by hand, and every beam a joke to the crowd.
Year after year the laughter grew louder. Men paced out the hull and shook their heads. Children threw clods of earth at the scaffolding.
For as in the days that were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark,
Feasts and weddings below, music in every camp. And up on the hill, one strange family still hammering.
Then the laughter turned to anger. Stones struck the hull. Ropes were cut on the scaffold. And still the ark grew taller.
When once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing,
Waited. Every hammer blow was one more day of mercy, even for the people throwing stones.
One night the crowd came up the hill with torches, shouting at the hull. And the old man on the scaffold did not answer them with words.
Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he.
No argument. No speech. Only obedience, one board at a time, until the last peg was driven.
At dawn it stood as it was told: a window above, a door in the side, three decks within. The valley that laughed went quiet.
Until the flood is over, Noah never speaks a word. Peter calls him a preacher of righteousness. His sermon was the ark.
Could you keep building while everyone you know laughs? Tell me in the comments.
The full story is in the long video. Part nine tomorrow: The flood.
